look_up_bin.description: Find out about a payment card from its first 6 to 8 digits (its BIN): the card network, whether it is a credit, debit or prepaid card, the bank that issued it and the country it comes from. Use it to spot a card from another country than the customer's, or to tell debit from credit before you charge. A whole card number can be given; only its first 8 digits are sent. No API key required.
look_up_bin.name: look_up_bin

parameters.description: The first 6 to 8 digits of the card, for example 45717360. A whole card number works too: spaces and hyphens are ignored, and only the first 8 digits are sent.
parameters.name: card_number

bank_phone.description: The issuing bank's customer service phone number, when CardBinCheck has it.

bank_website.description: The issuing bank's website, when CardBinCheck has it.

bin.description: The BIN CardBinCheck matched, which can be shorter than the digits looked up (42424242 matches 424242).

bin_searched.description: The digits that were looked up: the first 6 to 8 digits of what was given. The rest of a card number is never sent.

card_level.description: The card's product level, such as Classic, Gold, Platinum or Business. Empty when CardBinCheck does not know it.

card_type.description: Credit, Debit, Prepaid or Charge Card.

country_code.description: The two-letter code of the country the card was issued in.

country_name.description: The name of the country the card was issued in.

found.description: Whether CardBinCheck knows this BIN. When false, every card detail is empty and the message says why.

issuing_bank.description: The bank or financial institution that issued the card. Empty when CardBinCheck does not know it.

message.description: Why the BIN was not found or could not be looked up. Empty when it was found.

network.description: The card network, such as Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover or JCB.

look_up_bins.description: Look up a whole list of BINs or card numbers in one step, such as a column of payments, and get back each card's network, type, issuing bank and country, plus how many were found. A BIN that is unknown or mistyped comes back as a row saying so rather than failing the step. Up to 100 at a time, and it uses far less of the daily allowance than looking them up one by one. No API key required.
look_up_bins.display_str_template: Look up a list of card BINs.

results.message: This BIN is not in CardBinCheck's database.

look_up_bins.name: look_up_bins

parameters.description: Up to 100 BINs or card numbers. Only the first 8 digits of each are sent. Several in one entry, separated by commas or line breaks, are split apart.
parameters.name: card_numbers

count.description: How many BINs were looked up.

found_count.description: How many of them CardBinCheck knows.

not_found_count.description: How many were unknown or not valid card numbers.

results.description: One row per BIN, in the order they were given, so the rows line up with the list that was sent.

bank_phone.description: The issuing bank's customer service phone number, when CardBinCheck has it.

bank_website.description: The issuing bank's website, when CardBinCheck has it.

card_level.description: The card's product level, such as Classic, Gold, Platinum or Business. Empty when CardBinCheck does not know it.

card_type.description: Credit, Debit, Prepaid or Charge Card.

country_code.description: The two-letter code of the country the card was issued in.

country_name.description: The name of the country the card was issued in.

description: Look up a payment card from its first 6 to 8 digits (its BIN or IIN): the card network, whether it is credit, debit or prepaid, the issuing bank and the country it was issued in. Check one card or a whole list at once, to flag foreign cards or route payments. No account or API key required.
